name: Ui_PokerCards_ResetCardSlots
summary: Resets the poker card panel and its state object: sets the card mode, plays the open animation, clears the five card slots and the list selection, then rewinds the state words (0, -1, 1) and copies the two default words from the 0x0072A8A4 table.
evidence: NEW: the callees are now named and all belong to the poker panel - Ui_PokerTable_UpdateCardSlots (0x0023F514) and Ui_PokerWindow_SetAllCardVisibility (0x0023F5D0) on the same +400 card panel, plus Ui_List_SelectRow for the row deselect; the two callers are the panel-state steppers 0x001E30D8/0x001E3330. The state words are only offset-derived, which is why this stays at 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_SetIconFromList
signature: void maybe_Ui_Panel_SetIconFromList(u32* out, BattleUi* ui, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Sets the row icon of the poker panel from the entry under the list cursor: reads the entry through maybe_Ui_Entry_FillStyleParam, uses the special 4/0x0E icon or the entry's own icon id, then copies the two words of the 0x0072A8A4 table into out.
evidence: Still no caller, and the trailing copy of the 0x0072A8A4 words into out is unexplained (it looks like a vtable install, which does not fit an icon setter), so the role stays open. The icon half is supported by the two panel icon setters 0x0023F808/0x0023F844 and by the named entry reader maybe_Ui_Entry_FillStyleParam.

name: Ui_IconFlashing_RefreshState
summary: Re-applies the stored flashing flag of an icon: when the object reports ready (virtual +0x34) it plays the 'Flashing' animation (literal 0x00381C70) through virtual +0x84 if the flag byte at +0x220 is set, otherwise the idle animation at 0x00381C7C.
evidence: CORRECTED: the old name claimed an equip animation the body never plays. The adjacent entry 0x00381C14 is the confident Ui_IconFlashing_SetEnabled (0.55) and has the same shape - it stores the flag at +0x220 and then applies the same two literals; this function only re-reads +0x220 (ldrsb) and re-applies them, so it is the refresh half of the pair. The two 'callback addresses' the first pass saw are string literals in the literal pool: 0x00381C70 = "Flashing", 0x00381C7C = "Nut". No direct caller survives in the assembly, so the class label rests on the sibling.

name: Ui_Container_CollectFilteredChildren
signature: void Ui_Container_CollectFilteredChildren(int owner, LinkList* list, u32* out, int filterA, int filterB)
summary: Walks the intrusive child list of a UI container and appends every visible child whose vtable class id is neither of the two excluded ids to the caller's chain through func_0053CD1C, so the caller gets the filtered child set.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Ui_SenrekiWindow_DispatchEvent (0.55), and the body really does build the filtered set in *(out+4) - the two exclusions are the class ids 0x007AE89C/0x007AE8A0 compared against the child's virtual +8. The unaff_r5 in the readable C is only Ghidra's lost register for the list head, not damaged code, so 0.5 is safe.

name: Ui_PartySelectRowWidget_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the anim-ref row widget shared by the party-select and strength windows: installs the class vtable passed in r1, runs the shared Ui_DialogRoot_DtorBase and frees the object with operator delete.
evidence: CORRECTED: the old name said 'list row', and the first pass's caller was a mis-attribution - Ui_TsuyosaWindow_DtorBody (0x002A10B8) actually branches to the sibling 0x003B8AC0 (the non-deleting destructor) on an embedded member at -0x430. The class is fixed by the vtable: this entry is slot 1 of vtable 0x00768EAC, which is exactly the vtable the named Ui_PartySelectRowWidget_Ctor (0x003B8A80, 0.50) installs and the one 0x003B8AC0 re-installs. The disassembly is `str r1,[r0]; bl 0x29485C; b 0x10F6CC`.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor that only runs the shared non-deleting destructor 0x0028EFB4 and then frees the object; the disassembly is byte-identical to the confident Actor2D_EffectNode_DeletingDtor (0x0028EFA4).
evidence: CORRECTED: the old name said 'Field_Actor', but the cluster neighbours are the Field_SceneObject_DtorB/D/F/H/J family and the body is exactly `bl 0x0028EFB4; b 0x0010F6CC` - the same two instructions as 0x0028EFA4, which 31 classes share. No caller and no vtable literal, so the exact class stays open.

name: Field_Actor_RefreshModelVariantB
summary: Refreshes the actor's model variant: runs the shared model refresh, then picks variant 1 or 2 from bit 0x10 of the party member's flag halfword at +0xDA (variant 3 when self+0x43 is set), applies it with 0x005E7848 and finally asks the draw object at +0x204 for style 4.
evidence: NEW: the record lookup 0x0035EB98 is now the documented party-member getter (FACTS: func_0035EB98(work, idx) = party member record), so the variant choice is a member-state test on member+0xDA bit 0x10, not a random choice; the draw-object style call through vtable +0x54 is unchanged. The 'B' suffix is kept as the first pass's disambiguator - no sibling was found in this range.

name: maybe_Field_Object_DeletingDtor_vt77635C
summary: Deleting destructor of the small field scene object whose vtable is 0x0077635C: runs the shared Ui_Object_DtorBody and frees the object.
evidence: CORRECTED: the constructor that installs the same vtable 0x0077635C is now named maybe_Field_Object_Ctor_vt77635C (0.40, called from Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable), so the class is a field scene object, not a Ui_ValueHolder; the body is the standard deleting destructor (Ui_Object_DtorBody + operator delete).

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_EnsureTable
summary: Forces the lazy list-row table build: calls the alternate entry 0x00633560 of Ui_ListRow_BuildRowTable with the default 'initialized' flag and a row count of 8, and drops the returned record.
evidence: CORRECTED: the callee is not a text lookup. The disassembly is `bl 0x6F229C (Ui_GetCore); ldr r0,[r0]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x10]; mov r1,#8; bl 0x633560`, and 0x00633560 is the alternate entry of the confident Ui_ListRow_BuildRowTable (0x00633564, 0.55) that loads the default flag pointer and falls into the builder - so the 8 is the row count, not a text id.

name: Ui_SlotPlateWindow_UpdateStopSequence
summary: Steps the reel-stop sequence of the slot plate: waits for the running clip to finish, counts 10 frames, then switches the plate to the f_174 triple, plays the 'slot_stop' animation and copies the panel's value range from the 0x0072ABA8 constant block.
evidence: NEW: the animation name passed to the confident Ui_PlayAnimByName is the literal at 0x004C3540, which decodes to "slot_stop", and the body waits on the clip's own time field (f_4C[9]) before the 10-frame count - exactly the stop sequence the name claims.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_IsFieldActive
summary: Predicate in vtable slot 30 of the gadget class: returns the value the event-state getter 0x00636AFC reads from work->f_8->f_6C, which is zero when the work or the handle is missing. The readable body drops the returned value (Ghidra typed it void); it is a getter.
evidence: The twin 0x004C86D0 is identical and the class is fixed by the vtable neighbours Field_Gadget_Ctor_vt778438 / Field_Gadget_Dtor_vt778438, but 0x00636AFC is still not a decompiled entry point (it is a real function start that calls virtual slot 2 of the object at +0x3DC), so what 'active' means is open.

name: Ui_CursorWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the cursor/highlight sub-window: runs the generic slot sub-object constructor and installs vtable 0x00780B54.
evidence: NEW: the vtable it installs (0x00780B54) is the one whose destructor is already the confident Ui_CursorWindow_Dtor, and the body is the standard Ui_SlotSub_Ctor + vtable install, so the class label is no longer a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenObject_DtorDeleting_77C230
summary: Deleting destructor for the class whose primary vtable is 0x0077C230: installs the vtable, runs Ui_Object_DtorBody and frees the object.
evidence: The body is the generic deleting destructor (install vtable, Ui_Object_DtorBody, operator delete) and the companion entry 0x004EFCF4 installs the base vtable 0x0077D8BC, but no constructor installing 0x0077C230 was found and the xref caller Ui_Overlay_Dtor does not reference this entry in its body, so the class is still unidentified.

name: Ui_NumberPane_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the small number pane: destroys the base UI object and frees the allocation.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x0077C508 has the named slot Ui_NumberPane_Init (0x004F247C) and the matching Ui_Object_Ctor_vt77C508, so the class label is supported; the body is Ui_Object_DtorBase + operator delete. The xref caller Ui_SmithMenu_Dtor does not appear in that function's body, so it is a mid-function attribution and is not used as evidence.

name: maybe_Fs_StartAsyncRead
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_StartAsyncRead(int self, u32 handle, u32 length, u32 destination, u32 flags)
summary: Starts a read on an already-open handle: requires a 0x1000-aligned length and an idle object, stores the handle, sets the wait flag from bit 1 of flags, issues svc 0x1F on the handle and marks the request done on success.
evidence: The only caller is the thunk Fs_StartAsyncReadThunk, so the name is circular, and the body issues svc 0x1F (the blocking-wait slot of the CTR SVC table, between svcClearEvent 0x1E and svcWaitSynchronizationN 0x20) on the stored handle - so 'start async' may overclaim. The 0x1000 length alignment and the done flag at +0x18 are the hard facts.

name: Gfx_Y2r_SendGetStatus
summary: Sends the parameterless Y2R request 0x00260000 on the session at 0x007AEAAC and returns the status word the service writes back; the named caller Gfx_Y2r_WaitForCompletion polls it until the conversion reports done.
evidence: NEW: the body writes the request word 0x00260000 into the thread command buffer (the TLS pointer Ghidra prints as coproc_movefrom_User_R_Thread_and_Process_ID), sends it with svc 0x32 (svcSendSyncRequest) and returns the response word; the caller is the confident Gfx_Y2r_WaitForCompletion, which polls it - a get-status request, as the name says.

name: Ui_LayoutWindow_DtorBody
summary: Destructor body of the BFLYT 'wnd1' Window pane: installs vtable 0x00781554, frees the four child objects at +0xF4/+0xF8/+0xFC/+0xA4 and the 0xCE-entry pointer array, then runs Ui_Widget_DestroyChildren.
evidence: CORRECTED: the confident Ui_LayoutWindow_Ctor (0.90, the 'wnd1' Window pane constructor) installs the same vtable 0x00781554 and sits 0x18C bytes after this entry, so this is that class's destructor, not an 'AnimPlayer'. The body frees the children and runs the named Ui_Widget_DestroyChildren but never frees self, so it is the destructor body; the name avoids the existing Ui_LayoutWindow_Dtor (0x00605B1C), which installs a different vtable 0x0077F7C8.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DeletingDtor_vt782294
summary: Deleting destructor of a Gfx model-instance subclass: installs the derived vtable 0x00782294, frees the two derived heap blocks, then installs the base vtable 0x007828B0, runs Gfx_ModelInstance_FreeBuffers again, unlinks the three intrusive list nodes and frees the object.
evidence: CORRECTED: nothing in the body is text related. The second vtable it installs (0x007828B0) is exactly the one the confident Gfx_ModelInstance_Dtor installs, and both passes call the named Gfx_ModelInstance_FreeBuffers, so this is a model-instance subclass destructor; the derived vtable 0x00782294 has no named constructor yet, hence the _vt suffix and maybe_.

name: Ui_CriticalPopup_PlayAnim
summary: Starts the popup's appear animation when the widget is visible, the popup is open, no sub-state is active and its animation reference is idle: calls Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes on +0x9C.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x0077DAD8 has the named slot Ui_CriticalPopup_SetVisible and the body starts the animation through the confident Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes (0.5); the four guards are the only remaining uncertainty, and the sole caller is still maybe_ (0.45).

name: Battle2DUnit_GetAdjustedScreenPosition
summary: Returns the unit's stored display position (unit+0x19E8..+0x19F0) with x shifted by +0.5 or -0.5 depending on which side of the screen the model currently stands.
evidence: NEW: the confident caller Battle2DUnit_GetProjectedPosition (0x005A2768) uses it as the position source, and the body copies the three stored floats and shifts x by the 0.5 constant against the model's f_9C - the adjusted screen position the name claims.

name: Field2D_Bob_Update
signature: u32 Field2D_Bob_Update(float* bob, Field2DObject* obj, float deltaSeconds)
summary: Advances a looping vertical bob: adds the frame delta to the timer, and while the period has not elapsed writes the sine offset into the object's y position and returns 1; once the period elapses it writes the 4.0-based reset offset and returns 0.
evidence: NEW: the confident caller Field2D_Sprite_UpdateBob (0x005C9684) fixes the role, and the body is the timer -> sine -> obj->f_98 write the name describes. The frame delta arrives in s0 and Ghidra dropped it (FACTS: ARM hard-float s0 arguments), so the signature gains the delta parameter.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitComponentRecordPair
summary: Constructor of a gimmick variant: runs the shared base initialiser 0x005D451C, installs the derived vtable 0x00783FC8 and constructs the pair of 0x24-byte component records at +0xC4.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body is a constructor (base initialiser + vtable install + std_ConstructArray of two 0x24-byte records), and the class is fixed by the named Field_Gimmick_Dtor; nothing names the record type, so the old 'RectPair' claim is replaced by the project's Field_Gimmick_InitComponentRecord* wording.

name: maybe_Container_ReleaseObject
summary: Releases a Squirrel object container: installs vtable 0x0077F730, unlinks the object from its owner list when the linked bit is clear, destroys the embedded Sq_Stack at +0x18 and rewrites the child vtable at -0x18.
evidence: NEW: the embedded block teardown is the confident Sq_Stack_Destroy (0.8), so this is a Squirrel object-container destructor; the class itself is not named anywhere in the body and there is no caller, so the vague name stays.

name: maybe_BattleScene_LayoutPartyUnits
summary: Fragment of the battle-scene placement routine: only the std_ConstructArray setup of a 780-byte stack block over four 8-byte elements survives at this entry point, so the party-layout reading comes from the vtable slot (0x0077F9AC+0x3C), not from the visible body.
evidence: The single callee is the confident std_ConstructArray (0.7) and the vtable neighbours are BattleScene_UnitPlacement_Create/Dtor, which fits a four-slot party placement, but the actual placement walk is in the following block, so the precise name stays unsupported.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteObject_Dtor
summary: Truncated destructor of the sprite-object class: installs vtable 0x0077FBDC (+0x9C sub-vtable) and destroys the four 0x48-byte mesh entries at +0x298; the body then runs into data, so the base-class part is missing.
evidence: The vtable 0x0077FBE4 (this function is its first slot) also holds the confident Gfx_SpriteObject_CreateDefaultMesh (0.55), so the class is the sprite object; the body is cut off by halt_baddata() at the second vtable install, so the base-class half cannot be checked.

name: maybe_Object_ResolveEntryZero
summary: If the object has a container handle at +0xC, its type word at +0x38 is one of the three baked class constants 0x00286E68 / 0x00287794 / 0x00286D68 and its sub-index at +0x3C is 0, resolves entry 0 of that container through 0x007133F0.
evidence: CORRECTED: the callee is the real entry 0x007133F0 (not 0x00713344), which returns entry `index` of the container at *ptr, so the call resolves entry 0. The 'Ui_' prefix is contradicted by the verified caller Ui_ScreenFade_Setup (0x00368194) plus the unverified Monster_UpdateBehavior reference, and the three constants are compared against the type word at +0x38, so the object is not UI specific.

name: maybe_Object_ResolveEntryZeroB
summary: Second copy of the entry-0 resolution at 0x00632AF0: same three class constants, same container handle at +0xC and same 0x007133F0 lookup; Ui_ScreenFade_Setup calls both back to back.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body is byte-identical to 0x00632AF0 (same three constants 0x00286E68/0x00287794/0x00286D68, same +0xC/+0x38/+0x3C fields), so the earlier 'different kind family' story is wrong; the 'Ui_' prefix is dropped for the same reason as its twin.

name: Gfx_Pica_WriteTextureStateBlock
signature: u32* Gfx_Pica_WriteTextureStateBlock(void* ctx, u32* out, u32 arg3)
summary: Emits one 14-word PICA200 texture-state command block derived from the texture-unit bytes at ctx+0x164..+0x191 (enable/format bits, registers 0x000F008F, 0x000F01C0, 0x000F01C2, 0x000F01C3, 0x000F01C6, 0x000F01D9) and returns the advanced command cursor.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the confident Gfx_MaterialState_WriteAndCacheBlock, which appends this block and continues from the returned cursor; the body contains no float uniforms, so the earlier 'SetShaderUniforms' reading was wrong and the texture-state reading is the one the code shows.

name: Gfx_Pica_WriteTextureUnitBlocks
summary: For each of the eight texture units whose enable byte at ctx+i+0x164 is set, appends that unit's command block by calling 0x00657014 on its 0x2C-stride descriptor at ctx+i*0x2C+4, and returns the advanced cursor.
evidence: NEW: the caller Gfx_MaterialState_WriteAndCacheBlock (0x0065A0B0) really calls it in its body and continues from the returned cursor, and the eight-iteration loop over the per-unit enable bytes at ctx+0x164 is explicit; no LOD value is computed, so the old 'SetTextureLod' name was wrong. The other two xref callers (0x00655F58, 0x0065A66C) do not reference it in their bodies, so they are not counted.

name: maybe_Gfx_Node_InitInlineListA
summary: Stores {owner, owner+0x18} in the first two words of a large graphics node, then runs the inline member at +0xE0F8 through 0x005761D8 (named Os_ThreadObject_Dtor) and frees the block that call returns, adjusted back by 0xE0F8.
evidence: The callee is the confident Os_ThreadObject_Dtor, which clashes with the 'init' reading: either the callee's name or this function's role is wrong, and the body alone cannot decide. The vtable 0x00782668 neighbours (Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown, Os_ThreadObject_Dtor) do not name the class either.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_RebuildMoveController
summary: Rebuilds the movement controller at f_A0: when f_58 still points at the inline default (+0x50) it releases the old object and creates a new one from self+0x70 with the descriptor {0x0070D454, 0x0067121C, self}; otherwise it calls the sprite-node reset path.
evidence: NEW: the else branch is the confident Field2D_SpriteNode_ResetCallback and the f_A0 slot is also written by the tween-move factory at 0x00671B14, so f_A0 is a movement/controller slot; the builder 0x005BE5A8 is still unnamed, so the exact controller type is open.

name: maybe_Os_CacheBootQueryWord
summary: Caches one word in the global 0x007AF8E4: if it is still zero, calls the svc 0x21 wrapper 0x0010B210 and stores the returned word. Runs first in Os_InitMemoryManager, so the word is created during memory-manager bring-up.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x0010B210 is a five-instruction wrapper around `svc #0x21` (the SVC numbering is calibrated by 0x001112E0 = `svc #0x28` svcGetSystemTick and by FACTS' 0x23/0x24), so the cached word is whatever that SVC returns, not a boot parameter; the caller Os_InitMemoryManager only fixes the timing.

name: maybe_Snd_InitDspTimeouts
summary: Initialises the DSP state block at 0x007AEA00: sets the two default period values (+0x1C/+0x20), writes 0xFF into the two 16-bit fields at +4/+6, issues the DSP IPC command 0xC2 and, when it succeeds, sets the ready byte at +3.
evidence: The caller is the confident Engine_InitializeSubsystems and the block is the same 0x007AEA00 state that 0x00107208 tears down, but the DSP reading still rests on the IPC command (the named maybe_Svc_IpcCmd1100C2) rather than on a named service. The two fields at +4/+6 are written as 0xFF, not 0xFFFF as the first pass said.

name: maybe_Os_ShutdownSyncObject
summary: Tears the global sync object down: closes every registered handle through 0x0011C814, unlinks the node at 0x007E79D8, issues svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle) for the pending handle and clears the state word under the exclusive-access lock at 0x007AEA10.
evidence: The body closes the registered handles (svc 0x23), unlinks 0x007E79D8 and clears the state word under the exclusive-access lock at 0x007AEA10, but the object's identity is still unknown; the xref caller Input_Initialize does not reference this entry in its body, so it is a mid-function attribution and is not used as evidence.

name: maybe_Snd_StopVoiceGroup
summary: Stops and resets one voice group: releases the stream context 0x7F2C3C through 0x112E18, invalidates the four channel ids at +0x4C..+0x4F and clears the active byte.
evidence: The body is unchanged and the four -1 channel ids still fit one stream's four voices, but the current call graph has no caller at all (the first pass's 0x107628 is not a direct caller), so 'voice group' remains a label for the struct rather than something the code names.

name: maybe_Snd_GetCommandBlock
summary: Forwards the command-block getter 0x001129F4 and returns its result; the readable C shows `result = func_001129F4(); return result;`, so this is a getter, not a flush.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body returns the callee's result (Ghidra typed the thunk void and dropped it), so 'FlushChannelBlock' describes an action the code does not perform; 0x001129F4 is the command-block getter used by 0x00112848/0x00112888. No caller in the current graph.

name: maybe_Snd_SetMasterEnable
summary: Switches the driver's global output on/off: enable (arg 0) requires the ready predicate 0x0011E9B4 and arms the stream through 0x00118814; disable (arg non-zero) requires the current flag and stops it through 0x0011ECC0; the flag byte at 0x007AE910+4 is then updated.
evidence: The body arms the stream through 0x00118814 (enable) or stops it through 0x0011ECC0 (disable) and updates the flag byte at 0x007AE910+4, which fits a master on/off switch, but the owner is still inferred from that flag rather than from a named service; the xref caller Sound_Driver_BuildTwoEvents does not reference this entry in its body.

name: maybe_Gfx_WaitGpuEventLoop
summary: Polls the transfer command in a loop: each pass calls Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer with the context at 0x00119F7C, invokes the registered callback (table 0x00119F84, slot +0x48) when the returned event differs from the expected one, and ends on error or when the third stage reports the requested event.
evidence: The callee Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer is confident, which fixes the GPU-event framing, but the body is damaged decompilation (unaff_r9, in_ZR) so the exit condition and the parameter meaning cannot be trusted; kept at 0.3.

name: maybe_Mem_PoolInitFragment
summary: Mis-seeded Thumb entry decoded inside the pool-initialiser routine: the body is character-for-character the Mem_PoolInit prologue (four sub-buffer inits, the f_59 flag, the sentinel pointers), so it is a duplicate fragment rather than a function of its own.
evidence: The decoded body matches Mem_PoolInit 0x0011ADAC including the LAB_0011ae14 sentinel, and the entry address itself is suspect; the body is also damaged (coprocessor_store of cr7), so the name stays maybe_ at 0.3.

name: maybe_Snd_IpcCmd17
summary: Parameterless IPC request with the 0x0017xxxx command header (Ghidra printed the literal as an address into 0x00170000): writes the header into the thread command buffer, sends it with svc 0x32 and returns the response word.
evidence: The only caller is the resume path (Snd_RequestResume), the counterpart of the suspend path, so the 'resume message' reading holds; the exact header word had to be recovered from the disassembly and the service is still unnamed, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows(u32 cmdWord, u32 count, const u32* src)
summary: Appends raw texture rows to the GPU command list in chunks of at most 0x80 words: writes the header ((n-1)<<20)|0xF0000|cmdWord, copies the pixels (64-byte blocks through 0x0011CD00 where possible) and advances the global write pointer 0x007AED34; on overflow it resets the pointer to the buffer end.
evidence: The callers include the confident Gfx_LoadDefaultState and Gfx_UpdateTextureBindings plus the GPU-state builders, which fits a texture upload, but the same list also contains Sound_System_Shutdown, Sound_Decoder_DestroyChannels and Fs_Worker_Dtor, so either those names are wrong or the helper is more generic than 'texture rows'.

name: maybe_Field_CheckObjectState
signature: bool maybe_Field_CheckObjectState(FieldObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns the value the event-state getter 0x00636AFC reads from work->f_8->f_6C; when that value is zero it also invokes the object's virtual +0xC4 before returning. It returns a value (Ghidra's bool is right).
evidence: The only named callee is Os_GetGameWork and 0x00636AFC is still not a decompiled entry point (it is a real function start that calls virtual slot 2 of the object at +0x3DC), and there is no caller, so neither 'Check' nor 'ObjectState' is verified.

name: maybe_Actor_SubObject_ResetAndActivate
summary: Reset-and-activate handler of an actor sub-object (sole slot of vtable 0x0072BD8C): resets the base state, re-shows every child of the +0x180 list, drains the pending-animation counter, re-links the embedded node and sets the sub-widget state to 1.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body starts with Actor_SubObject_Reset and then re-links and activates, so 'Finish' described the wrong end of the transition; it is the same template as the 0x002FDxxx/0x00307xxx family. The class is only known from the vtable literal, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_ActionWindow_Reset2
summary: Reset variant of the shared window template: drains the pending children, re-links the embedded node, resets the base parts, sets the sub-widget state to 1 and raises the flag at +0xBC8.
evidence: The body only re-links and re-activates (the same template as the Ui_Window_InitAndActivate family) and destroys nothing, so 'Reset2' is a placeholder; no caller identifies the window class.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InitAndActivateA
summary: Window bring-up/reset variant A: resets the base-window parts, drains the pending-child list, re-links this window's list node at +0x344C and re-enables the sub-widget at +0x288.
evidence: The tail callees are now named (Ui_Object_SelectEmbeddedNode, maybe_Ui_ToggleLabel_SetState) and confirm the reset/re-link/activate sequence, but four window classes share the body and nothing identifies this one.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InitAndActivateB
summary: Variant B of the same sequence: marks every child row active (bit 0 of +0x44), raises the two state flags f_188 and f_208, then drains the child list, re-links the +0x344C node and enables the +0x288 sub-widget.
evidence: Same template as variant A with two extra flags; no named caller distinguishes the owning window class, so the lettered placeholder stands.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InitAndActivateD
summary: Variant D: byte-for-byte variant B minus the f_208 flag - resets, marks the child rows active, sets f_188, drains the list, re-links the node and enables the +0x288 sub-widget.
evidence: Same shared template; only the flag subset differs, and no caller identifies the window class.

name: maybe_Ui_Pane_StartAnimFrame15
summary: Starts animation track 15 on the pane referenced by f_18 and passes the frame number from f_10 (packed as frame<<16) to the pane's animation call.
evidence: The caller is the confident Actor_SubObject_Reset and the constants are confirmed (track id 0xF, frame<<16), but the two callees 0x00648B7C and 0x00382A80 are still unnamed, so what track 15 animates is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetAndActivateA
summary: Teardown/reset template variant A: drains the child list, re-links the +0x344C node, resets the base parts and raises the object's +0xAB8 state flag.
evidence: CORRECTED: nothing in the body is text related and the trailing 0x0029126C call is a state setter, not a free, so both 'Text_Block' and 'Dtor' were wrong; the body is the shared reset/re-link/activate template.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetAndActivateB
summary: Reset template variant B: drains the children, re-links the +0x34D8 node and resets the base parts, then on the lazily created shared 0x80-byte object returns whether the low two flag bits are both set and sets bit 1 in the companion flag word when they are.
evidence: CORRECTED: the flag test (~obj[0x1A] & 3) == 0 is real but neither the object nor the flags are named, and the first half is the same template as the other variants, so 'Text_Block' and 'Font' were unsupported. It returns a value; callers ignoring it are Ghidra's dropped returns.
